scholarships.title: VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington

existing.description: The VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship is a partial fee-based scholarship of NZ$15,000 towards tuition fees for one year of study, for new international students entering their first year of a Bachelor's degree programme at Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington and studying full-time on campus. No separate scholarship application is required: eligibility is assessed when the student applies for their programme, and the outcome is communicated in the Offer of Place. The scholarship is credited directly against tuition fees upfront, is awarded formally once the student enrols in first-year courses, and covers one year of study only. Students completing Victoria's EAP or Foundation Studies programmes remain eligible, but returning students, Study Abroad or Exchange students, students with credit transfer, government sponsored students and holders of domestic status are not. Withdrawal after award can trigger repayment, and a change in fee or residency status from international to domestic can cause the scholarship to be withdrawn, suspended or repaid.
eligibility: Be an international student who is paying full international fees
Intend to study towards a Bachelor's degree at Victoria University of Wellington
Hold an unconditional or conditional Offer of Place for a Bachelor's degree at Victoria University of Wellington
Be a new student to Victoria University of Wellington
Not be already studying at Victoria University of Wellington as a returning student, unless undertaking the University's EAP or Foundation Studies programmes
Not be a Study Abroad, Exchange or Twinning student from an overseas partner university
Not have received credit transfer, advanced standing or recognition of prior learning from a previous qualification
Not be sponsored by their home government or the New Zealand government
Not be an Australian or New Zealand citizen, permanent resident, resident visa holder, or hold a diplomatic visa entitling them to domestic status
existing.eligibility_summary: International students paying full international fees who intend to study towards a Bachelor's degree at Victoria University of Wellington, hold an unconditional or conditional Offer of Place, and are new students to the University. The scholarship is open to students completing or recently completing Victoria's EAP or Foundation Studies programmes, but not to returning students, Study Abroad or Exchange students, students with credit transfer or advanced standing, government sponsored students, or Australian and New Zealand citizens, permanent residents, resident visa holders and diplomatic visa holders.
benefits: NZ$15,000 tuition fee credit applied directly to tuition fees upfront, so students pay the reduced amount to the University
Applies for one year of study only, for the student's first enrolment in the programme
May be held in conjunction with other scholarships where the other scholarship's conditions permit
Recipients may request approval to defer the scholarship to another intake within the same calendar year
coverage: NZ$15,000 credited towards tuition fees only, for one year of study
requirements: Apply for a Bachelor's degree programme and hold an Offer of Place
Enrol in first-year courses, which is when the scholarship is formally awarded
documents: Application for a Bachelor's degree programme at Victoria University of Wellington, through which eligibility is assessed
Evidence of international fee status and of the Offer of Place, held by the University
existing.english_requirement: Not stated as a separate scholarship requirement; students completing Victoria's English for Academic Purposes (EAP) or Foundation Studies programmes are explicitly eligible for the scholarship.
application_method: No separate scholarship application: students are assessed for scholarship eligibility on application for their programme
Recipients are advised in their Offer of Place if the scholarship has been offered
existing.selection_notes: Holders must demonstrate their academic potential, as demonstrated by their admission into a Victoria University of Wellington programme. The official page describes no separate competitive selection round; eligibility is assessed through admission.
existing.best_fit: New international students entering the first year of a full-time on-campus Bachelor's degree at Victoria University of Wellington who are paying full international fees.
existing.duration: One year of study only, for a student's first enrolment in the programme
existing.application_period: Aligned with programme applications; there is no separate scholarship application window and the outcome is communicated in the applicant's Offer of Place
existing.deadline_display: Closing date(s): Same as the programme application closing date. A scholarship application is not required; students are assessed for eligibility on application for their programme.
existing.program_type: Partial tuition fee scholarship for new international undergraduate students

existing.description: Tulī Takes Flight scholarships are funded by the New Zealand Ministry of Education and administered by the Pacific Education Foundation to reduce financial barriers to tertiary study and vocational training for Pacific people. They form part of the government's gesture of goodwill and reconciliation to Aotearoa Pacific communities following its 2021 apology for the Dawn Raids. Awards can be made for either vocational or academic study and can run for one, two or three years. For the 2027 round the Ministry states applications are closed and outcomes will be notified by 18 March 2027; a new annual round is expected to open in the same late-summer window each year.
eligibility: Have enrolled or be in the process of enrolling into full-time training or study with a tertiary provider in New Zealand; part-time study is not eligible
Be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident
Have lived in New Zealand for the last three years
Be of indigenous Pacific cultural heritage
Have completed NCEA 3 (or equivalent) and be 16 years or over by the time the course starts; or, if already out of secondary school, be 18 years or over

For a new to study or training award: not have done more than half a year of equivalent full-time tertiary education, meaning 0.5 EFTS or 60 credits at Level 3 or above on the NZQA framework, including equivalent tertiary education in any country
For a continuing study award: have successfully completed at least 1 year of study, or be expecting to enter a second or subsequent year of training or study
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be enrolled or in the process of enrolling in full-time study or training with a New Zealand tertiary provider, be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, have lived in New Zealand for the last three years, be of indigenous Pacific cultural heritage, and have completed NCEA 3 or equivalent and be 16 or over when the course starts (or 18 or over if already out of secondary school). New-to-study applicants must have done no more than 0.5 equivalent full-time student load of tertiary education; continuing-study applicants must have completed at least one year of study or be entering a second or subsequent year.
benefits: Tuition fees covered for full-time study
Course materials and equipment costs covered
Help with living costs including accommodation, transport and childcare
coverage: Full-time course costs such as course materials, equipment and tuition fees
Help with living costs such as accommodation, transport and childcare
application_method: Read the official Tulī Takes Flight scholarship application guide before submitting
Apply online using the Tulī Takes Flight application form published on the Ministry's scholarship page
Applications not supported by the correct documents are considered incomplete and will not be assessed
existing.selection_notes: Decisions about awarding the scholarships are made by the Pacific Education Foundation Board and are final. The Board informs all applicants by email of the outcome and provides general feedback, but is unable to give individual feedback on applications. A quarter of scholarships are targeted to priority pathways.
existing.best_fit: New Zealand citizens or permanent residents of indigenous Pacific cultural heritage who have lived in New Zealand for three years, are entering or continuing full-time tertiary or vocational study in New Zealand, and meet the NCEA 3 and age requirements.
existing.notes: For the 2027 round a quarter of the scholarships awarded are targeted to priority pathways: STEM, health and allied health, digital, data and AI, engineering and skilled trades, training, research and education workforce, and green, climate and sustainability fields. The remaining scholarships continue to support the full breadth of study including social services, construction, Pacific languages, and Pacific customs and culture. The Tulī programme is distinct from the separate Pacific Education Foundation scholarships and from the Tulī career changer strand.
existing.application_period: Annual round for study in the following year. The 2027 round closed at 11.59pm on Wednesday 30 September 2026, with outcomes notified by 18 March 2027. The next round is expected to follow the same pattern but no date is published yet.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for the 2027 round are closed. The Ministry's official page states "Applications for the 2027 round are now closed" and "You will be notified of the outcome of your application by 18 March 2027". The round closes annually on 30 September at 11.59pm; no date for the next still-applicable round is published on the page as at 2026-10-04.
existing.program_type: Government-funded scholarship for Pacific students, administered by the Pacific Education Foundation
